Subject: Allowlist / firewall needs for on-prem private endpoint (Horizon POC)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for walking through the private endpoint option for our POC. Horizon's Security and NetOps teams have a couple of items we need to finalize before we can spin up connectivity on our side:

- Canonical list of outbound destinations (IPs and FQDNs) to allow from our private subnet to Redwood control and inference planes (we need both TCP ports and protocol expectations).
- Whether TLS with SNI is required or if IP-only TLS is supported for the control plane.
- Any known dynamic IP ranges (CDN, provider-managed) vs static appliance IPs.
- If Redwood requires direct outbound NAT vs support for egress proxy (we run a transparent proxy for auditable egress).
- Minimum monitoring/audit requirements (syslog, flow logs) to satisfy our compliance review.

I've attached a CSV template (horizon-mvp-allowlist-template.csv) for us to fill. Can you provide the initial matrix and any specific firewall exemptions (if any) you recommend? We aim to complete the list and get a change window next week.

Appreciate it — if it's easier, happy to book a 30-minute call with NetOps/security.

Best,
Alex Chen

Horizon Analytics

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear checklist and the template. Putting Irene (Infra) and Kimberly (Security Ops) on copy so we can provide the authoritative matrix. High-level notes while they draft the spreadsheet:

- We expose two logical endpoints for private deployments: a Control plane endpoint (management, metrics, rollouts) and a Data/Inference egress endpoint (real-time token streaming and payloads).
- Control plane: mostly HTTPS 443, mutual-TLS optional depending on Private vs Dedicated. We prefer SNI + TLS; IP-only TLS can be supported but requires a short exception and our cert pins.
- Inference/data plane: outbound from your VPC to our inference egress IPs on TCP 443. We support routed proxies; however, we do require consistent source IP NAT visibility for entitlements and rate-limiting.
- We will provide a static set of IPs for the initial POC; longer-term some auxiliary services (metrics ingestion, CDN) are via dynamic ranges — we'll call those out so you can decide whether to allow FQDN-based rules or explicit ranges.

Irene / Kimberly — can you take Alex's template and populate the exact IPs, ports, FQDNs, and recommended firewall rules? Also indicate any exceptions for proxies and what audit logs we need to capture on Horizon's side.

Thanks,
Aditya
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 07:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Allowlist / firewall needs for on-prem private endpoint (Horizon POC)

Alex —

Attached is the completed matrix (redwood-egress-ip-matrix.xlsx) and a short design note (egress-fallback-flow.pdf). Summary of the key requirements and rationale below so your reviewers can have a quick read:

1) Control plane (management / config / rollouts)
- Destinations: 3 static IPs (include in spreadsheet) and control.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS 443).
- TLS: TLS 1.2+ required; SNI expected. We publish certs via ACM; if you prefer IP-only TLS, we can provide cert thumbprints for firewall pinning but that path bypasses our CDN (minor performance hit).
- Auth: OAuth client credential flows over HTTPS; no inbound ports required.
- Firewall rule type: outbound allowlist to Control plane IPs/FQDN. Rationale: low cardinality (static) and tied to management.

2) Inference / Data egress - Destinations: two ranges for the inference egress pool (static for POC) plus a small set of CDN endpoints for artifact/weights fetch. Details in spreadsheet.
- Ports: TCP 443. Optional port 80 for health/legacy; we recommend blocking 80 except for temporary artifact downloads noted per the matrix.
- Connectivity model: NAT through your egress gateway is fine; however, the source IP we see must be consistent for the lifetime of a session for model-telemetry association. If you use an intermediate proxy that rewrites source IPs, include an audit mapping (original IP to proxied IP) or preserve X-Forwarded-For.

3) Proxying and TLS interception - We support egress proxies. Please ensure TLS interception (MITM) only occurs with strict cert pinning coordination — Redwood will need to validate the proxy cert chain or you should enable passthrough for our FQDNs. If Horizon requires TLS inspection for compliance, we can sign a temporary cert or provide an allowlist to bypass inspection for inference/control FQDNs.

4) Dynamic ranges / CDN - Artifact fetching uses a CDN (third-party) with some dynamic IP ranges. For POC we will provide a snapshot of the ranges and recommend allowing by FQDN with short TTL DNS resolves on your firewall. For long-term, we will propose putting artifact fetch behind a dedicated artifact proxy (option to avoid dynamic firewall changes).

5) Audit and logging expectations - Horizon should ingest VPC flow logs + firewall logs to central SIEM. For SOC/contractual audits we will request: egress flow logs covering IPs/ports, TLS SNI, and timestamps for a 90-day window. For emergency forensics, flow logs with 365-day retention will be requested (per contract addendum).

6) Exceptions and escalation - We try to avoid firewall "exemptions" but permit narrow, time-bound exceptions for IP-only TLS or temporary port 80 usage. Exceptions require a RFC with justification, expiry, and owner. We will treat any exemptions as a security risk and require approval from Redwood Security (kimberly_park@redwood.com).

Next steps:
- See attached spreadsheet: column "POC_ALLOW" = yes/no; please return with your approval or modifications.
- If you'd like, we can run a short connectivity test: we supply a small test container that performs a TLS handshake and posts a short payload to our inference endpoint so you can validate NAT/pinning behavior.

For quick reference the spreadsheet includes: source_port (outbound), dest_ip_or_fqdn, protocol, purpose, ttl_recommendation, proxy_notes, redwood_contact.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Infrastructure — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
